headline: Elemental Energies wins Viking CCS engineering contract from Harbour Energy
summary: Harbour Energy awarded UK subsurface-and-wells specialist Elemental Energies a contract supporting the Viking CCS project in the Humber — the depleted-gasfield CO2 store (targeting ~4 Mtpa, rising toward 10 Mtpa by 2030) that Harbour operates (60%) with bp (40%). The engineering/wells scope advances the project as it works toward FID and first injection later this decade.
co2crc_note: Viking is a flagship UK depleted-field CO2 store; wells/subsurface engineering milestones there are directly comparable to CO2CRC's depleted-reservoir storage work.
extractor_note: No contract value disclosed in source snippets. Story carried by 5 outlets (Energy Voice, Carbon Herald, Marine Technology News, World Pipelines, Upstream) all dated 10 Nov 2026 via Google-Alerts sampler. headline: Occidental beats Q3 estimates and flags new CO2 offtake deals for enhanced oil recovery
summary: In its third-quarter 2026 results Occidental beat analyst estimates and disclosed new CO2 offtake agreements tied to enhanced oil recovery, reinforcing its dual-track low-carbon strategy spanning the Stratos DAC facility in the Permian (via 1PointFive) and CO2-EOR offtake.
co2crc_note: US CO2-EOR offtake economics and DAC commercial progress are a reference point for CCS revenue models, though peripheral to CO2CRC's dedicated-storage focus.
